scenario: AITA for not wanting to be friends with my group anymore? | So I just finished my freshman year in college, and I found myself a pretty good friend group. I’ve always been really shy so the fact that I‘m part of a group means a lot to me. However, I’m the only one (in a group of 8) that is not in our school’s Honors College. Many people, including them, have assured me that this doesn’t mean they’re smarter than me or harder working than me, and I’ve accepted that. However, Honors College people all have some required courses to take that are just for them, so they all have classes together without me. And sometimes when we hang out, everyone talks about their classes and I feel completely left out. In addition, I found out that next year, they’re all living in the Honors College dorm building together. I can’t live there since I’m not in Honors College and I already feel left out enough. Now that they’ll all live together, it’s even more likely they’ll end up hanging out without me just because they’re all living together and just happen to run into each other and how can I blame them for that?? I have tried to talk to a couple of them about it and one in particular said that I have no right to make them feel bad for being happy that they can live together but I feel like if they had an ounce of empathy, they’d realize that 7 people of an 8 person group living together is rather unfair. I don’t want to have to start over and find new friends but I also feel like I deserve friends who will try to include me. AITA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's AITA (Am I the Asshole) for not wanting to be friends with my group anymore. Let me break this down step by step. First, I just finished my freshman year in college and found a good friend group. That's awesome because I've always been shy, so being part of a group means a lot to me. But here's the thing: I'm the only one in the group of eight who isn't in the Honors College. People, including my friends, have told me that this doesn't mean they're smarter or harder working, and I've accepted that. So, on the surface, it seems like we're all on the same page about that. However, the Honors College students have required courses that are exclusive to them. This means they all have classes together without me. When we hang out, they talk about their classes, and I feel left out. That's understandable because when everyone else is sharing experiences that I can't relate to, it's easy to feel excluded. Then, I found out that next year, they're all living in the Honors College dorm building together. I can't live there because I'm not in the Honors College. This makes me feel even more left out. They'll be living together, which means they'll probably hang out more without me just because they're all around each other. I get that they might not intentionally exclude me, but the situation makes it more likely. I tried talking to a couple of them about how I feel. One person said I have no right to make them feel bad for being happy about living together. That stung because I was hoping for some understanding or empathy. I feel like if they had an ounce of empathy, they'd realize that having seven out of eight people living together is unfair. I don't want to start over and find new friends, but I also feel like I deserve friends who try to include me. So, is it AITA for me to not want to be friends with them anymore? Let me think about this. On one hand, I'm feeling excluded because of circumstances beyond my control—their classes and living arrangements. It's natural to feel left out when the group dynamics shift in a way that makes it harder to be included. On the other hand, they're not doing anything wrong by living together or talking about their classes. They're just being part of their own community. But I'm also considering whether I'm being unreasonable. Maybe I'm expecting them to make an effort that's not feasible, especially since they're all living together. It's a lot to ask for them to include me when they're so close by proximity. However, I do feel like I deserve some consideration. If they truly care about our friendship, they might make an effort to include me despite the challenges. I'm also thinking about whether I'm the one being the asshole. Am I overreacting? Maybe I'm projecting my feelings of inadequacy onto them because I'm not in the Honors College. But I've already accepted that they're not smarter or better than me, so that shouldn't be the issue. The issue is more about the practical aspects of their lives making it harder for me to be part of the group. In the end, I think it's not AITA for me to feel this way. It's valid to feel excluded and to want friends who make an effort to include me. However, I also need to consider whether it's realistic to expect them to change their living arrangements or habits just for me. It might be time to look for new friends who are in a similar situation or who can better accommodate my needs.
